question: Rulers of Mahajanapadas in ancient India collected taxes on crops at the rate of _____ of what was produced.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1/6th**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Building forts** and** keeping massive armies** were among the mahajanapadas' chief pursuits in order to safeguard their **realm and their people**.
 
• They required **more funds,** which** taxes **could provide.
 
• The most significant taxes were those on **agriculture.**
 
• Typically, the tax was set at **1/6th of the output.**
 
• It was referred to as** bhaga or sharing.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• In ancient India, there were** sixteen kingdoms **collectively known as the **Mahajanapadas.**
 
• The late **Vedic period's tribes (janas) **decision to establish their own** territorial communities** marked the beginning of everything.
 
• As a result, new, long-lasting communities known as** "states" or "janapadas"** gradually arose.
 
• Buddhist sources state that **Majjhimadesa i**s the owner of the **first fourteen** of the aforementioned Mahajanapadas.
 
• The** final two,** however, are a part of **Uttarapatha,** which is **Jambudvipa's northwest region.**
 
• There were just** 4 strong kingdoms** left in the 6th century:
 
 
• Magadha
 
• Avanti
 
• Kosala 
 
• Vatsa ​
